To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The -GDG- motif of the thiamin dphosphate (ThDP)-binding site of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDC) is critical for ThDP binding.

the aspartate of the -GDG-motif is essential for binding the ThDP cofactor, that the glutamate of the -GDGGD- motif is essential for binding ThDP and Mg 2+, that the second asparatge of the -NN-motif is required for binding ThDP, and that the conserved prolyl residue is not essential for activity.
the -GDG-, -E-, -N- and -NN- sequences are required for the binding of ThDP to PDC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the residues within the ThDP-binding domain in cofactor binding, enzyme activity and protein stability.
the role of the conserved residues of the ThDP binding site in PDC.
the role of the elements in the putative ThDP binding site of PDC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conserved -GDG-, -NN- and -E- residues are all essential for ThDP binding, while the -P- residue is important for maintaining the tertiary structure.
the -GDG-, -NN-, glutamate and proline residues are required for ThDP binding and Mg2+ activation of PDC.
the -GDG-, -NN- and -E- residues are all important for cofactor binding, but that the -P- residue is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the -GDG-, -GG-, -NN- and the -GG- sequences of the ThDP binding motif are all required for the binding of ThDP to the enzyme, but that the conserved glutamates and the proline residues are not essential for the binding and catalytic function of the enzyme.
the conserved aspartate and asparagine residues are important for cofactor binding, whereas the glutamate and the proline are not.

the conserved residues in the -GDGN- sequence are important for cofactor binding, while the -GDGNN- sequence is important for both cofactor binding and the maintenance of the quaternary structure of this enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a conserved motif of 30 residues, including a -GDG- triplet and an -NN- sequence, is required for the binding of ThDP by PDC, with the -GDG-, -GN- and -NN- residues being essential.
the ThDP binding motif is not sufficient for ThDP binding and that other regions of the protein may play a role in binding ThDP.
the -GDG-, -NN- and -GG- motifs are essential for ThDP binding and that a conserved glutamate residue is also required for ThDP binding.
